newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Megawati supporters in peaceful protest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Megawati supporters in peaceful protest.

text.p: The first organised opposition demonstration in Jakarta in six months, by supporters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, passed off on Thursday without incident.
About 300 supporters handed over petitions at parliament and national police headquarters, before chaining and spray-painting the gates at the official residence of her political rival.
Police kept in the background, guiding the demonstrators' motorcade along the city's main thoroughfare. A handful of troops kept well back from the final protest site.
"This is just the beginning. There will be follow-up protests that will be much larger," one of the organisers, Suparlan, told Reuters.
The number of demonstrators was far below the 2,000 to 3,000 that leaders had predicted for the protest, the first such demonstration in Jakarta since July 27 riots rocked the city.
Political observers had said the turnout could give some idea of opposition power in the run-up to general elections at the end of next May.
About 300 demonstrators gathered in the morning at parliament and handed a petition to the head of the public relations section after top officials refused to receive them.

The demonstration was called to demand authorities investigate the activities of deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi, who replaced Megawati as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) at a government-backed rebel congress in June.
President Suharto has given Surjadi his seal of approval, and only members of his faction have been approved to run for the PDI in the May elections.

The July riots, in which at least five people died and dozens of buildings burned or were damaged, were sparked by an attack by Surjadi backers on the PDI headquarters occupied by loyalists of Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's founding president Sukarno.
Police charged 124 Megawati supporters with disobeying orders and refusing to disperse, but made no move against Surjadi's backers in the attack on the PDI building.
Last month, 115 of those arrested were released after serving four months in jail. Nine others were acquitted.
Thursday's petition called on the government to take appropriate action equally against both PDI groups.
It called for the temporary suspension of Surjadi's faction in parliament and demanded that Megawati supporters be allowed to contest the elections.
The demonstrators drove from parliament for about four km (2.5 miles) to the national police headquarters, where a police lieutenant-colonel received the petition.

They then moved on to Surjadi's official residence, where about a dozen riot police in the garden stood back as the protesters chained the main gate and sprayed Megawati's name in red paint on the gate posts.
The demonstrators strung up a black banner with the words "This house is sealed by the people" in white before dispersing quietly.
The "symbolic" sealing of Surjadi's house was an apparent reference to the closure by local government authorities of Megawati's temporary offices in east Jakarta in September.
